chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The pre-dawn meal (suhur) is a blessing."
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Let my ummah not abandon the pre-dawn meal, even if it is just a sip of water."

key_terms.السَّحُورُ: The pre-dawn meal eaten before fasting begins
key_terms.حَشَفَةٍ: A sip or small drink of water

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of suhur in Shia Islamic tradition and why is it considered a blessing?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores Suhur not merely as a physical necessity but as a distinct spiritual act of worship (ibadah) that invites divine mercy. The Prophet’s instruction to maintain it even with a 'handful of dates' (hashafah) highlights the emphasis on consistency and intention over the quantity of food, reinforcing its status as a highly recommended practice (mustahabb) for the Ummah.
